context: Your host sends you to the supermarket with a shopping list. Labels are full of kanji, so today you learn to find things and get through the checkout.

phrases.jp: {卵|たまご}はどこにありますか。
これは{豚肉|ぶたにく}ですか。
phrases.note: Useful if you avoid some meats: {牛肉|ぎゅうにく} beef, {鶏肉|とりにく} chicken.
Bags cost a few yen. The cashier asks {袋|ふくろ}はご{利用|りよう}ですか.

phrases.jp: ポイントカードはありません。
phrases.en: I don't have a points card.
phrases.note: You'll be asked this in almost every shop.

phrases.jp: これ{半額|はんがく}じゃん！
phrases.note: じゃん = casual "isn't it!". Evening half-price bentos are a budget traveller's friend.

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.jp: いらっしゃいませ。ポイントカードはお{持|も}ちですか。
dialogue.en: Hello. Do you have a points card?

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.jp: {袋|ふくろ}はご{利用|りよう}ですか。

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: いいえ、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。

dialogue.speaker: Cashier
dialogue.jp: お{弁当|べんとう}、{温|あたた}めますか。
dialogue.en: Shall I heat up the bento?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: はい、お{願|ねが}いします。

kanji.where: Printed on every food package, with a date like 26.11.20 (year.month.day).
kanji.related: Related: {消費期限|しょうひきげん}, the stricter use-by date on fresh food.

tip.title: Shop late for discounts
tip.body: An hour or two before closing, staff put stickers on bentos, sushi and bread: {2割引|にわりびき} (20% off), then {半額|はんがく} (half price). Locals know the timing. After paying, you pack your own bags at a separate counter.

challenge.prompt: You can't find the milk. Ask a staff member: "Excuse me, where is the milk?"
challenge.model_answer: すみません、{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}はどこにありますか。
